title: xv6 kernel extensions
description: Extensions to the educational xv6 RISC-V kernel, exploring processes, memory, and system calls.
results: Additional system-call definitions include scheduler switching, process timing, and waiting for a process ID.
The process structure includes running, ready, sleeping, and termination timing fields.
proof: Added scheduler-switching and process-timing system calls.
context: This project extends MIT’s educational xv6 operating system. Working inside a small RISC-V kernel makes process state, scheduling, and the boundary between user programs and the kernel directly inspectable.
contribution: Extended kernel interfaces for scheduler switching and process timing. The public source includes additional system-call definitions and per-process timing fields.

architecture.summary: User programs reach kernel functionality through system calls. Process state and accounting live in the kernel’s process structures.

decisions.title: Build on a teaching kernel
decisions.description: The work extends the existing xv6 codebase. The original operating system belongs to its upstream authors; the contribution is the extension work, not authorship of the kernel.

decisions.title: Expose behavior through system calls
decisions.description: Explicit interfaces make scheduler selection and process timing accessible from user space while keeping the underlying process structures inside the kernel.

decisions.title: Track process states separately
decisions.description: The process structure contains running, ready, sleeping, and termination timing fields. These make state accounting inspectable without claiming a measured scheduler-speed improvement.

limitations: Educational kernel work, not a production operating system. This case study does not claim benchmark improvements or a complete verification of kernel correctness.
resourceNote: The repository includes xv6 build instructions requiring a RISC-V toolchain and QEMU. There is no browser-based demo.
